correctness.rationale: The cuboctahedral graph is constructed exactly as the line graph of the cube, with verified 12 vertices, 24 edges, diameter three and unique antipodes. Adams--Shukla--Singh Lemma 2.2 gives complete even/odd Čech facets. At scale two the 248 faces admit a fully checked 120-pair acyclic matching with one critical zero-cell and seven two-cells (732 Hasse incidences). At scale three the 1100 faces admit a fully checked 547-pair matching with one critical zero-cell and five three-cells (4644 incidences). Forman discrete Morse theory then gives integral sphere wedges because each CW skeleton below the critical dimension is a point. Scale four is the exact boundary of the 11-simplex, scale five the full simplex. Scale one is the 12-vertex 24-edge connected graph, giving 13 circles. Distinct positive homology degrees in successive stages give the claimed complete integral persistence barcode. The actual standalone package verifier reproduces facet enumeration, DAG checks and independent mod-two boundary ranks. No finite rank experiment is substituted for the integral homotopy proof.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedron is a canonical Archimedean polyhedron and its graph is the natural line graph of the cube, making intrinsic Čech persistence a motivated benchmark distinct from its Euclidean Rips filtration. The full integral homotopy sequence includes nontrivial degrees two, three and ten and complete birth/death information, together with a sharp non-shellability diagnosis at both middle scales. Exact exhaustive acyclic matching certificates supply structural topology beyond tabulating homology ranks; no broad theorem or downstream application is claimed.
